question.prompt: Build one program that takes the robot to the door. Use as few steps as you can, then press RUN.

acceptedEquivalence.note: Alternate optima exist (mirror routes, equal-cost turn orders, and repeat/flat token forms). A submission is CORRECT iff its expanded action sequence never bumps a wall or edge, steps on every key, and ends on the door. It is OPTIMAL iff, in addition, its action count equals cost.actions. Token economy is judged separately against cost.tokens and only when instructionSet.repeat.enabled.
acceptedEquivalence.efficiency: M-EFF = cost.actions / executedActionCount (1.0 = optimal, capped at 1.0)

solved_optimal.rationale: the program runs without a bump, collects every key and stops on the door, using exactly the optimal number of primitive actions (correct + maximally efficient)

solved_detour.rationale: a legal solving program that uses more actions than the optimum (route or turn inefficiency; M-EFF < 1)

solved_verbose.rationale: action-optimal but uses more program tokens than optimal (repeat counts not exploited; instruction-set inefficiency)

crashed.rationale: a forward step ran into a wall or off the grid; the run aborts at that action (planning/simulation failure)

missed_key.rationale: the robot stopped on the door but never stepped on one or more keys (goal decomposition failure)

incomplete.rationale: the program ended somewhere other than the door with no crash (under-planned route)

A submission is CORRECT iff its expanded action sequence never bumps a wall or edge, steps on every key, and ends on the door. It is OPTIMAL iff, in addition, its action count equals cost.actions. Token economy is judged separately against cost.tokens and only when instructionSet.repeat.enabled.
acceptedEquivalence.efficiency: M-EFF = cost.actions / executedActionCount (1.0 = optimal, capped at 1.0)

solved_optimal.rationale: the program runs without a bump, collects every key and stops on the door, using exactly the optimal number of primitive actions (correct + maximally efficient)

solved_detour.rationale: a legal solving program that uses more actions than the optimum (route or turn inefficiency; M-EFF < 1)

solved_verbose.rationale: action-optimal but uses more program tokens than optimal (repeat counts not exploited; instruction-set inefficiency)

crashed.rationale: a forward step ran into a wall or off the grid; the run aborts at that action (planning/simulation failure)

missed_key.rationale: the robot stopped on the door but never stepped on one or more keys (goal decomposition failure)

incomplete.rationale: the program ended somewhere other than the door with no crash (under-planned route)
